source.title: Urban Futures: October workshop findings
source.audience: Research partners, community organizations, and local policymakers
source.cta: Review the draft findings at the November follow-up session.
source.source:
The fictional Urban Futures project completed its first round of community mapping workshops in October 2026. Across three workshops, 48 residents shared how they use public spaces and where they encounter barriers to access.

Participants identified a need for more shaded seating, accessible footpaths, and welcoming spaces for intergenerational activities. These are preliminary qualitative findings from the workshop participants, not a representative survey of the city.

The research team will now organize the anonymized workshop notes into themes and invite participants to review the draft findings. A follow-up session is planned for November 2026. No policy commitments or measured improvements have been established at this stage.

source.title: Skills for Change: learning materials review
source.audience: Research partners, community organizations, and local policymakers
source.source:
The fictional Skills for Change team has completed a co-design session with community facilitators. Participants reviewed a draft learning pathway focused on job-search confidence, interview preparation, and practical digital skills.

The next step is to revise the learning materials using the feedback. The pilot has not started, and no employment outcomes have been measured.

source.source:
The fictional Open Research project is preparing an online methods exchange in November 2026. Researchers and community partners will discuss how to make qualitative research methods easier to understand and reuse.

The agenda is being developed. The final date, registration link, and speakers will be announced after confirmation.
